content.title: EasyJet says summer bookings rising after wider quarterly loss
content.summary:
STORY: British budget airline easyJet said summer bookings were building strongly, despite reporting a wider first-quarter loss on Thursday.

The company has been hit by expansion costs and soft winter pricing.

Winter is typically the weakest period for airlines.

Carriers rely on spring and summer demand to lift earnings.

The company said the busy January booking period has seen record levels in both volume and revenue ahead of summer 2026. 

But the airline reported an operating loss of around $105 million in the three months to December 31.

That's compared with around a $55 million loss a year earlier.

Despite this, the airline kept its 2026 outlook unchanged with shares rising 2% in early trading.

Separately, Wizz Air reported a third-quarter operating loss in line with expectations.

Earlier this week, larger rival Ryanair raised its fare growth outlook after a strong start to 2026 bookings.

Budget carriers have sidestepped many of the challenges facing Europe's biggest airlines.

Which have been squeezed by weaker transatlantic travel linked to tariff threats from U.S. President Donald Trump.

content.title: EasyJet exploring Starlink Wi-Fi deal, but economics not right yet
content.summary: EasyJet has held talks with Elon Musk's Starlink about offering ​on-board Wi-Fi, but the economics do not ‌stack up for the British budget airline at the moment, ‌Chief Executive Kenton Jarvis said on Thursday.  "At ​the moment ... where we are with our talks ‌with Starlink, the economics aren't quite working for us," Jarvis told journalists in a post-earnings call, though he added that the product was a "really good one", with fast streaming speeds.
